interactables.name: Derek
interactables.altText:
[Derek] has the headphones down around his neck for once, staring at the wall like it owes him sleep.
'You are still working? At night? In a house full of adults?' A long pause.
'Respect.'
interactables.text: The Husband, [Derek], stands beside the bed in brand-new noise-canceling headphones, radiating the deep peace of a man who has finally solved his one problem.

topics.prompt: Paw at his trailing audio cable
topics.text:
He lifts one ear cup with two fingers.
'[Something heavy rumbled] through downstairs earlier this evening - the entrance hall, then the living room. Around [seven]. Maybe later. Wheels, anyway. Dinner cart, probably - the maid does her run at seven.' He considers the ceiling.
'Didn't look. Wasn't my problem.' The ear cup goes back down.

topics.prompt: Stare at the headphones until he explains
topics.text:
'What? Everyone copes differently.' He taps the box on the nightstand.
'That bird screamed at five every morning. I went through a whole drawer of [foam earplugs] first. Useless. So I left Viv a note - [do something] about that bird, I wrote. She did not. So I did something myself. Legal. Non-violent. Three hundred dollars.' He looks briefly, profoundly at peace.

He does not flinch. Not even a little.
'See? Nothing. Three hundred dollars well spent.' He taps one ear cup, smug as a sealed jar.
'Exactly one thing has ever gotten through these: that bird, at [eight o'clock] tonight. A [squawk, straight through the noise canceling]. You know what that tells me? Wherever that bird went, he was still around at eight. Loud and alive.' He resettles the headphones like a crown.
'Case closed. Goodnight.'

keywords.displayText: squawk, straight through the noise canceling

topics.prompt: Knead the duvet beside him, thoughtfully
topics.text:
He watches you knead. He does not stop you.
'You know what is funny,' he says slowly, 'now that somebody with whiskers asks. That rumble downstairs. It came [twice] this evening. Same weight, same wheels - and the kitchen only ran one cart.' He frowns for the first time all evening.
'Strange. But the bird squawked at eight, straight through my headphones. So he was still AROUND at eight... right?' The frown stays.

interactables.name: Delivery Manifest
interactables.text:
A crew manifest on the dresser, entries all evening:
- Florist, out - 6:10 PM
- Catering ice run - 6:55 PM
- [R. - dinner service] - [7:00 PM]
- '[2x equipment cases]', hurried scrawl - 7:00 PM
- Linen return, housekeeping - 7:10 PM
- [Grip dept., lamp returns] - [7:20 PM]|Half the house rolled through this wing inside one hour. Every entry carries a readable name - except one [scribble with a tail]. It could belong to almost anybody.
A collected dinner tray waits on the dresser: [soup bowls scraped clean], silverware squared away. The dinner cart came through this wing on schedule, then, and somebody ate well.

interactables.name: Derek's Note
interactables.text:
A handwritten note on the nightstand:
'Viv - Rudebeak woke me up at 5AM. AGAIN. Do [SOMETHING] about that bird or I will. I am [past asking] nicely.' - D.
An open box for top-of-the-line noise-canceling headphones, a spare [audio cable] still coiled in the foam. Purchase receipt inside: [yesterday's date]. Someone finally [snapped].

localDeductionSentence: [Derek] heard a [rumble] downstairs - it lines up with the [dinner service] due at [seven], but also with the [two mystery cases] the paperwork wheels into the wing. Only one sound has ever beaten his [headphones]: the [squawk], at [eight]. So the bird was still around at that time... right?
